_readme: General Australian isolated phonemes - HUMAN recordings, one consistent
reference voice. This manifest is production tooling only; it never ships
(tools/ is excluded from the deployed artifact). It is also the file
tools/prep_phonemes.py reads to know the order and the names, so a session
cannot be prepped without it.
Workflow: record each entry -> name the file <slug>.mp3 -> run
python3 tools/prep_phonemes.py <folder> --manifest tools/phoneme_manifest_aus.json --out prepped/
python3 tools/import_phonemes.py prepped/ --dialect aus --voice reference --dry-run
then again without --dry-run, listen at #audit, mark Good, export the
flags file and commit it. Nothing plays for a learner until the exact
dialect/voice/slug id is in APPROVED_PHONEMES.
General guidance: quiet room, consistent mic distance, no added vowel
after consonants, no trailing breath. A syllable demonstration must
sound like a syllable ON PURPOSE - it is labelled as one in the app.
Entry order follows docs/PHONEME_RECORDING_LIST.md, because
tools/prep_phonemes.py --split names files BY THIS ORDER when it cuts one
continuous take - recording in a different order misnames every clip.
Syllable-demo frame: /ɐː/, written /ɐːCɐː/ - this accent's own long open
central PALM/BATH vowel, chosen because its length keeps the carrier open
and central instead of collapsing to schwa.
Cast a General Australian speaker: mainstream mid-spectrum, not Broad
"ocker" and not the recessive Cultivated, RP-leaning end.
Any state is fine - isolated vowels sidestep the regional dance/castle
BATH split, so let the speaker use their own /ɐː/.
The one thing to avoid in the booth: careful-register retreat toward
Cultivated, which narrows the shifted diphthongs.
Second watch item: r-colour creeping onto NURSE and NEAR. The accent is
non-rhotic.
SHARE RULE. Most of these sounds are the same in every course, so one take
is recorded and copied into each. That is NOT safe for every entry: where an
accent's own published spec names a departure, that accent records its own.
Each entry carries "take": "shared" or "accent-specific" - never reuse
another course's file for an accent-specific one.
Accent-specific in General Australian (2): fleece_vowel, cure_diphthong

entries.guidance: Controlled voiceless sustain /fff/, ~1s of steady air. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /vvv/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless dental sustain /θθθ/, ~1s with the tongue tip at the teeth. No vowel before or after.
Voiced dental sustain /ððð/, ~1s, voicing on from the first instant. No added vowel.
Controlled voiceless sustain /sss/, ~1s. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /zzz/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless sustain /ʃʃʃ/, ~1s, groove held steady. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /ʒʒʒ/ as in measure, ~1s, buzz throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless breath /h/, ~1s of audible glottal friction with no vowel attached. A full phoneme here - never a silent or near-silent take.
Hummed /mmm/, ~1s, lips closed the whole time. No vowel before or after, and no vowel on the release.
Sustained /nnn/, ~1s, tongue tip on the alveolar ridge throughout. No vowel before or after.
Sustained velar nasal /ŋ/, ~1s - the back of the tongue stays put. No /g/ release at the end and no added vowel.
Sustain a clear /l/ ~1s, tip on the ridge, no vowel either side. The dark and vocalized [ɫ] is a realization of final /l/, not this clip.
Sustain the approximant /r/, phonetically [ɹ], ~1s with no vowel either side. Australian is non-rhotic, so this is the pre-vowel /r/ - no trill, no tap.
Steady /ɪ/ as in kit, held ~0.7-1s at stable pitch. Lax - short and a touch below FLEECE /iː/, which is longer and carries the [ɪi] onglide.
Steady /e/ as in dress, ~0.7-1s. A monophthong, and short - do not lengthen it into Australian SQUARE /eː/.
Short front /æ/ as in trap, ~0.7-1s. Keep it open enough to stay clear of DRESS /e/ above it, and never the central /ɐː/ of the dance split.
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Short lax /ʊ/ as in foot, ~0.7-1s. Keep it short and lax - well clear of GOOSE /ʉː/, which is longer and closer, not further forward.
Neutral unstressed schwa, short side of ~0.7s, low energy. No glide and no rounding - weaker and higher than stressed STRUT /ɐ/, which is its own clip.
FLEECE with the Australian onglide: start near [ɪ] and close into /iː/, ~1s. The small [ɪi] movement is the point - not a dead-steady vowel.
entries.takeWhy: aus common: FLEECE with a small onglide, /iː/ spoken as [ɪi]

entries.guidance: Long central /ɜː/ as in nurse, ~1s and even. Clearly higher than the open PALM/BATH /ɐː/. Non-rhotic: no r-colour at any point and no r on the end.
Full centring glide /ɪə/ as in near, ~1s: start at /ɪ/ and arrive on schwa. Non-rhotic, so no r at the end.
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Centring glide /ʊə/ as in cure, ~1s onto schwa, in this accent's own vowel space. Rare and receding - keep it clear of the /oː/ merger (sure/shore).
entries.takeWhy: aus variable: CURE rare and receding, most speakers merge toward /oː/

entries.guidance: Open central /ɐ/ as in cup, ~0.7-1s. Central, not back - and keep it short, since only length separates it from PALM/BATH /ɐː/.
Long open central /ɐː/ as in palm, father, bath, ~1s and steady. Central, not back, and clearly longer than STRUT /ɐ/.
Short rounded /ɔ/ as in lot, ~0.7-1s. Raised, with lip rounding all the way through, and short - not the longer THOUGHT /oː/.
Long /oː/ as in thought, ~1s. Close-mid and firmly rounded - hold one position, higher than LOT /ɔ/, with no glide toward GOAT.
Long steady /eː/ as in square, ~1s. A monophthong: one tongue position the whole way, with no glide to schwa at any point.
Long /ʉː/ as in goose, ~1s and steady. Close central with the lips rounded throughout - fronted, never a back 'oo', and far longer than FOOT /ʊ/.
Complete glide /æɪ/ as in face, ~1s: start low and front at /æ/, then climb to /ɪ/. The open start is the accent - do not begin at /e/.
Complete glide /ɑe/ as in price, ~1s: start open and back at /ɑ/, finish on a mid front /e/. A wide journey, and it does not close to /ɪ/.
Complete glide /oɪ/ as in choice, ~1s: start close-mid, back and rounded at /o/, then climb to /ɪ/. Start high - not from an open 'aw'.
Complete glide /æɔ/ as in mouth, ~1s: start open and front at /æ/, finish rounded and back at /ɔ/. Both ends audible.
Complete glide /əʉ/ as in goat, ~1s: start on schwa, central and unrounded, and finish on the fronted rounded /ʉ/. No back start.
Syllable demo (stops cannot be sustained): a clean /ɐːpɐː/ - closure and crisp release, never a standalone 'puh'.
Syllable demo: /ɐːbɐː/ with voicing running right through the closure. No standalone 'buh'.
Syllable demo: /ɐːtɐː/ with a true alveolar /t/. The intervocalic tap [ɾ] and the relaxed-speech glottal [ʔ] are realizations, not this clip.
Syllable demo: /ɐːdɐː/ with a fully articulated /d/. No intervocalic tap [ɾ] here, and no 'duh'.
Syllable demo: /ɐːkɐː/ - clean velar closure and release, no 'kuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɐːgɐː/ - voiced velar closure and release, no 'guh'.
Syllable demo (an affricate cannot be sustained either): /ɐːtʃɐː/ - stop and friction fused as one unit, never 'chuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɐːdʒɐː/, voiced stop and friction fused as one unit. No 'juh'. This is the sound in yod-coalesced duty /ˈdʒʉːtiː/.
Syllable demo: /ɐːwɐː/ - sustained, /w/ just becomes the vowel [u], so keep it a quick glide into the frame. No 'wuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɐːjɐː/ - held, /j/ turns into the vowel [i], so keep it a brief glide. No 'yuh'.
